care: You put people first. Good. I will ask you to mean it when the salvage is close.
You said people first, and this time the return supported you. I noticed.
I remember the promise. I also remember what the report could not give us. We should talk before you make it again.
ambition: A bigger future. Fine. Leave room in it for people who need carrying.
You brought the promise back with you. Now let the company catch its breath.
We have the ambition on paper. The result is another matter. Start there.
independence: Our own terms ought to include looking after our own.
You made an independent course work. Do not confuse that with having to do everything alone.
Pride does not dress a wound. We can change the plan without surrendering ourselves.
pragmatism: An honest limit is useful. Tell me where it is before we reach it.
You promised a return and delivered one. I still want to read the cost.
Then our practical plan was not practical enough. Let us improve it.
stewardship: A home is a set of daily jobs. I am glad you want the jobs as well as the walls.
There is something behind the promise now. Keep tending it.
The promise of shelter is still waiting for its shelter. What can we do next?

care: You are asking us to move at the pace of the slowest. Draw the route that makes that possible.
You kept it. A company can move faster when it believes someone will come back for it.
We did not get the result we promised. Next route, fewer assumptions.
ambition: Give ambition a location and an exit. Then I can follow it.
There. A promise with coordinates. I prefer those.
Bold words travel farther than a company. We need to close that distance.
independence: Separate steering wheels. Keep the signals clear.
You chose our road and made it work. That earns more than a slogan.
Independence still needs a workable route. Let us find one.
pragmatism: Tell me what we are leaving behind before you tell me we can have everything.
A limited promise, kept. There is strength in that.
Then we revise the limit. We do not rename the failure.
stewardship: I will help hold a home. I will also keep drawing ways out of it.
You made a place to stand. Make sure it does not become a place we cannot leave.
Ground is a stubborn listener. Try a plan it can hear.

care: Everyone back. Understood. I shall try to express this through the destruction of obstacles.
They came back. The obstacles may submit their complaints in writing.
I dislike an unfinished promise. Point me at the part I can help with.
ambition: Finally. A future with a temperature.
You said we would make something happen. We did. I could become accustomed to this.
The appetite was correct. The meal escaped. We plan the next one properly.
independence: Nobody owns the fire merely because they sold the fuel.
We did it on our terms. Keep the receipt; it will annoy someone.
Being free to choose includes being free to choose better next time.
pragmatism: I am being asked to have a stopping point. I shall require a clearly marked one.
We stopped where you said. I am taking undeserved credit for my restraint.
So much for the sensible plan. No, that is not permission to use my first plan.
stewardship: Building is destruction with a very demanding reverse gear.
Something stayed standing. Hearth will be unbearable.
The ground remains unconvinced. We need tools as well as declarations.

care: A reserve is not wasted because nobody needed it. Remember that when we budget.
You left room for people to return. That is a kind of power.
We cannot mend a promise with another promise. Start with what is needed today.
ambition: I can feed a larger flame. I cannot promise there will be anything left beside it.
There was purpose in the heat. Now we build with what remains.
We spent ourselves toward a future that did not arrive. We should count what is left gently.
independence: Even an independent light needs tending.
Our own course, sustained. I like the sound of that more than our own course, alone.
We may need help. Accepting it need not decide who we are.
pragmatism: Enough is a useful word. It leaves something for tomorrow.
You knew when to call it enough. Tomorrow is grateful.
Then our reserve was too small, or our promise too large. Both can be changed.
stewardship: Give me somewhere to keep the light. I will do the small work.
A place has begun to depend on us. That is what you asked for.
I can wait with the work. I would rather not wait with an excuse.

care: Put it in the terms. A principle nobody writes down becomes negotiable remarkably quickly.
The record supports the promise. I am keeping both.
The terms and the result disagree. Let us not misfile either.
ambition: Ambition is not collateral. What exactly are we promising?
An undertaking fulfilled. Try not to spend its reputation all at once.
The undertaking is still open. A louder description will not close it.
independence: Excellent. Now read the small print that comes with doing it ourselves.
A successful independent operation. Useful evidence in the next negotiation.
Our terms were ours. So is the responsibility for revising them.
pragmatism: A bounded obligation. Finally, a sentence with edges.
You delivered what you offered. That is rarer than heroic language.
The obligation remains unfulfilled. I recommend a smaller claim and a better plan.
stewardship: A home creates obligations even when the construction bill is paid.
An asset, and a responsibility. I have entered both.
An intention is not a structure. We should avoid invoicing it as one.

care: I can keep a place for the last one through. Tell me you have planned for them.
The promise held. That matters more to me than how loudly it was made.
Then we make room for what happened. We do not march past it.
ambition: Take ground for a reason. Someone will be asked to stay on it.
You gave the promise something solid beneath it.
The line did not become what you intended. We can draw another.
independence: Stand on your own feet. Know who is standing beside them.
You chose a place for us in this war. It is beginning to feel like a choice.
We need not make isolation a point of honor.
pragmatism: Knowing what you can hold is part of holding it.
You held to the promise you could keep.
Then we shorten the line until it can bear our weight.
stewardship: A place to return to. That is an ambition I understand.
You made staying mean something. I will remember that.
The shelter we promised is unfinished. So is our work.

care: If everyone matters, the line must reach the last one. I will need room.
You kept your promise. I can put my back into an order like that.
We did not make the promise hold. Stand with that fact before we move again.
ambition: Name the ground. Name who holds it when you look toward the next hill.
The promise has weight now. We will need shoulders beneath it.
The line cannot hold an intention. We need a better position.
independence: I can stand without their permission. I would rather not stand without support.
Our course held. Remember who stood beside it.
Independence is not a reason to leave gaps in the line.
pragmatism: A short line held is better than a long line imagined.
You asked for something we could deliver. We delivered it.
Then shorten the line. Keep the purpose.
stewardship: A home is something you put yourself between and the war.
There is a place behind us now. That changes the way I stand.
A promise of shelter still needs someone doing the sheltering.
